The volume equation is
\[
80a+42b=1540 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 40a+21b=770.
\]
Modulo \(21\), \(40a\equiv -2a\), so
\[
-2a\equiv 770\equiv 14 \pmod{21}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad a\equiv 14 \pmod{21}.
\]
Thus \(a=14+21k\). Then
\[
b=\frac{770-40(14+21k)}{21}=10-40k.
\]
Nonnegativity forces \(k=0\), so
\[
(a,b)=(14,10).
\]
This gives \(14+10=24\) bricks.

This packing is possible: split the box into a \(10\times 8\times 14\) slab and a \(10\times 3\times 14\) slab. Place \(14\) bricks of size \(2\times 5\times 8\) in the first slab by orienting them as \(5\times 2\times 8\), giving \(2\cdot 7\cdot 1=14\) bricks. Place \(10\) bricks of size \(2\times 3\times 7\) in the second slab by orienting them as \(2\times 3\times 7\), giving \(5\cdot 1\cdot 2=10\) bricks.

Therefore the only possible total number of bricks is

\[
\boxed{24}.
\]
